status_note: Reproduces on 2.0.0, the latest release; on main (d4eea3f208, 2026-11-06) `least.cpp` still sends `FLOAT` through the sort-key path, read in the source. No upstream issue: duckdb#14239 (closed) is about NULL and NaN order, not the sign.
title: `least` and `greatest` on `FLOAT` turn `-0.0` into `+0.0` and drop a NaN's sign
summary: `least` and `greatest` on `FLOAT` return a value that is none of their arguments when the winner is `-0.0` or a negative NaN: they compare sort keys and decode the winner from its key, which encodes both zeros alike and every NaN as the positive quiet NaN. So `least(-0.0::FLOAT, -0.0::FLOAT)` is `+0.0`. On `DOUBLE` they keep the argument (`least(-0.0, -0.0)` is `-0.0`, `least(-0.0, 0.0)` is `-0.0`), so the two widths disagree.
repro: `SELECT signbit(-'nan'::FLOAT), signbit(least(-'nan'::FLOAT, -'nan'::FLOAT)), signbit(least(-'nan'::DOUBLE, -'nan'::DOUBLE))` gives `true, false, true`.

The same from table columns: `CREATE TABLE t AS SELECT -0.0::FLOAT f, -0.0::FLOAT g, -0.0::DOUBLE d, -0.0::DOUBLE e; SELECT signbit(least(f, g)), signbit(least(d, e)) FROM t` gives `false, true`. (`least(f, f)` is simplified to `f` and keeps the sign.)
handling: No effect on sverify's results: the reference has one zero and one NaN, and sverify's SQL normalises `-0.0` to `0.0` (duckdb-R14, duckdb-float-signs).
